summary: A time of day typed into hour, minute and AM/PM segments in the reader's own format, taking and returning a 24-hour HH:MM string.
useWhen: the user sets a time of day — a schedule, a reminder, the start of a window
any minute is allowed, so a list of choices would be long or would leave times out
beside a DatePicker when the value is a date and a time; the two sit side by side and share one box

useInstead.when: only a handful of times are allowed — delivery slots, office hours
useInstead.why: picking from four slots is a choice from a list, and a field that accepts any minute invites times the product will refuse

useInstead.when: the value is a duration — 30 minutes, 2 hours
useInstead.why: a duration is an amount, not a time of day; 02:00 as a length reads as two in the morning

useInstead.when: the value is a calendar date

hour.use: on-the-hour schedules — the minute segment is not shown

minute.use: the default — almost every time of day a person sets

second.use: logs and precise triggers; the value becomes HH:MM:SS

guarantees: each segment is a spinbutton that announces its own name, value and bounds — 'hour, 2, minimum 1, maximum 12' — and takes digits or arrow keys
each editable segment is its own tab stop, like DatePicker and the native time input; the separator is not
the 12 or 24-hour clock, the separator and the AM/PM wording come from the reader's locale, so '2:30 PM' and '14:30' are the same field and the same value
the segments sit in one labelled group, so the name is announced once on entry
a time that does not exist cannot be typed
a time outside `minValue`/`maxValue` turns the field invalid and names the bound in the reader's own format, without `isInvalid` — the value is kept, not silently clamped
requires: `label`, or `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
a `description` saying which timezone the time is in, whenever the reader could be in a different one from the thing being scheduled
notes: `value` is a wall-clock time with no date and no zone. Keep the timezone as its own field or setting; a time pinned to a `Date` drifts an hour at every daylight-saving change.
The clock icon is decorative. There is no dropdown of times: two digits are faster to type than 96 quarter-hours are to scan, and a list makes 09:07 impossible.

antiPatterns.dont: passing a Date, a timestamp or a locale-formatted string such as "2:30 PM" as `value`
antiPatterns.why: the value is 24-hour HH:MM. A malformed value throws with the prop name rather than rendering an empty field
a reader whose locale uses 24 hours has to translate every value, which is the misreading the segments exist to prevent. Leave it to the locale

antiPatterns.dont: a schedule time with no timezone anywhere on the form
antiPatterns.why: "09:00" is nine o'clock somewhere; if the reader and the workspace are in different zones, they will each assume their own

antiPatterns.dont: using `minValue` and `maxValue` for a window that crosses midnight
antiPatterns.why: 22:00 to 02:00 has a minimum later than its maximum, so every time is refused; validate the window yourself and set `isInvalid`
